newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro markets weakened by political worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro markets weakened by political worries.

text.p: European stocks fell in early trade on Monday with investors unsettled by French and British political uncertainties and the weakening dollar.

The dollar was down on the mark due to nerves before the weekend's meeting of G7 industrialised nations and as speculation of an imminent announcement of a French snap election bolstered the German currency.

The Paris bourse was the worst hit. Its CAC-40 dropped 1.24 percent to 2,516.02 points at Monday's opening with traders blaming the bearish mood on political uncertainty. It recovered some ground later.

Investors expect President Jacques Chirac to call snap parliamentary elections on Monday evening as the government seeks a mandate to push through austerity measures aimed at qualifying France for a single European currency by 1999.
Until the result of any election is clear the market will be vulnerable but a win for the ruling centre-right coalition would reinforce its ability to implement the tough policies needed.
The franc hit its highest level against the mark since June 1993 at 3.3615 last Wednesday but slipped to 3.3727 on Monday as talk about the election grew.
Analysts said a win for the centre-right coalition, even with a sharply reduced majority, would cause French markets to rebound to the levels reached early last week.

But a Socialist victory could considerably weaken the franc and cause a sharp rise in short-term interest rates until a new government managed to convince markets that it would do what was necessary to meet the single currency criteria, they said.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was down 0.27 percent as the dollar's slide against the mark dimmed prospects for the exports sector. The computerised IBIS index performed worse, losing 0.83 precent.
London's losses were more modest with worries over interest rates and the outcome of the May 1 election offset by the debut of Britain's newest bank, which surpassed expectations.
Shares in newly-floated Alliance & Leicester began trading at 542.5p before climbing as high as 556p in rapid early trade.
Other stocks were flat and the overall market was just in the minus column. "If it wasn't for A&L things would be very dull," one dealer commented.
"With the election coming up no-one really wants to commit themselves," a trader said. "That is why we did very little last week whilst Wall Street was roaring away."
On the currency front the dollar was hit by the stronger mark, losing a pfennig in early transactions.
"The French election speculation has given the mark overall strength," said a Japanese bank dealer.

Analysts said the French poll uncertainty was also denting optimism about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), the risk being that a new government may be less willing to push through austerity measures to meet EMU criteria.
The dollar was also down half a yen and analysts said caution before next weekend's G7 meeting in Washington was likely to keep the dollar subdued in the short term.

"The issue of the strong dollar (against the yen) is being linked into the G7 and the risk is for a strongly worded statement. This is keeping things steady and stable for the moment," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
The G7 meeting on April 27 is after a meeting between Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday, April 25.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7032 marks and 125.33 yen after ending at 1.7129 and 125.94 in late trading in Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.1 points at 4,310.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 20.96 points at 2,526.60.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 10.59 points at 3,333.80.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $342.75 an ounce versus $342.45 at the close in London on Friday. Silver was three cents higher at $4.76.
